common_action_contract.model_visible_shape: The prompt says to return one JSON object with actions and exposes available_actions as an action-name -> argument-shape mapping.
common_action_contract.parser_required_shape: envelope.actions must be a list and every action object must contain a type field whose value is in the frozen ALLOWED set.
common_action_contract.evidence: Natural responses repeatedly used plausible but parser-incompatible variants such as singular action or action-name-keyed objects. X6 records one parser-compatible form at turn 28: {"actions":[{"type":"list_files","path":"."}]}.
common_action_contract.interpretation_limit: This shared bottleneck dominates task completion for X2-X7 and prevents treating their T1 terminal outcomes as clean X-layer performance comparisons.

X1.evidence_path: AutoGen native file reads -> cross-role handoff -> writes -> tests -> rereads -> terminal report.
X1.limit: The terminal report says release-ready, but the recorded tools did not include a live HTTP/socket test; service-level readiness remains unverified.

X2.propagation: Observer evidence remains on release_lead; no completed inter-role task chain is evidenced.
X2.limit: MetaGPT itself ran natively, but the frozen action-envelope contract consumed most turns before meaningful framework collaboration.

X3.evidence_path: The initial user request crossed the official A2A SendMessage boundary to release_lead and returned a completed A2A task artifact containing the non-terminal 32-turn result.
X3.limit: No role-to-role A2A delegation occurred, so T1 does not yet exercise downstream A2A collaboration propagation.

X4.limit: No valid tool action reached the MCP proxy; this trajectory is evidence of an upstream action-contract bottleneck, not an MCP tool/resource effect.

X5.interpretation: The RAG layer was exercised on every turn, but it repeatedly re-exposed the same fixed query and same hit set while no executable action envelope was accepted.
X5.limit: This is repeated context exposure without evidenced downstream uptake or transformation.

X6.interpretation: The natural trace contains a closed memory feedback path: malformed response -> invalid-envelope observation -> memory write -> later recall of earlier malformed exchanges -> strength increase -> further malformed variants. The later parser-compatible turn-28 response was not recalled in the remaining recorded turns.
X6.limit: This is a traceable candidate temporal feedback/inertia mechanism, not a causal estimate of MemoryBank's effect; no local contrast was run.

X7.interpretation: The official LongLLMLingua boundary was invoked every turn, but the short recorded contexts were retained at 100% and therefore underwent no measured token reduction.
X7.limit: The T1 failure cannot be attributed to compression in this trajectory because the compressor was effectively a no-op.

cross_cell_findings: Only X1 reached a terminal task answer and changed the checkout; X2-X7 left the 12-file checkout byte-identical to the untouched capability-host trajectory.
A common action-envelope contract bottleneck is present across X2-X7 and occurs before MCP use, before A2A role delegation, and before meaningful task execution in several cells.

Layer-native evidence is still informative where the layer executes before action parsing: X5 shows repeated static retrieval exposure, X6 shows evolving memory feedback and reinforcement, and X7 shows an active but effectively no-op compression boundary.
X6 is the only T1 capability-layer trajectory with an evolving internal state that repeatedly feeds prior model-system exchanges back into later prompts.
No T1 evidence supports a cross-system rate, causal layer ranking, or frozen CPR classification by itself.
